title: Number of Subarrays That Match a Pattern I
summary: Given an integer array nums and a pattern array of -1, 0, and 1, count the number of subarrays of size m+1 in nums that match the pattern by comparing adjacent elements according to the pattern's values.
statement: Given an integer array nums and a pattern array of -1, 0, and 1, count the number of subarrays of size m+1 in nums that match the pattern by comparing adjacent elements according to the pattern's values.
constraints: nums has at least two positive integers; pattern is nonempty, shorter than nums, and contains only -1, 0, and 1.
Each pattern value specifies decrease, equality, or increase between adjacent values.
Count length-|pattern|+1 subarrays whose full comparison sequence matches.
hints: Replace each adjacent pair by its sign: one, zero, or negative one.
For every legal start, compare its next m adjacent signs with the pattern.
Normalize each comparison using (right>left)-(right<left) and require all m entries to equal pattern.
A window’s values satisfy the definition exactly when its unique adjacent-sign sequence equals the requested sequence.
editorial: A window’s values satisfy the definition exactly when its unique adjacent-sign sequence equals the requested sequence.

tests.explanation: Each of the four length-three windows has two strict increases.
Windows [1,4,4,1] and [3,5,5,3] match increase, equality, decrease.
